definitions.explanation: The Japanese punctuation mark (・) placed at the center of the line, used to separate items in a list, mark boundaries in katakana words, or indicate an abbreviation.

examples.japanese: {中黒|なかぐろ}で{区切|くぎ}る。
カタカナの{人名|じんめい}は{中黒|なかぐろ}で{姓|せい}と{名|めい}を{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: In katakana names, an interpunct separates the surname and given name.

examples.japanese: {並列|へいれつ}する{語|ご}を{列挙|れっきょ}するとき、{読点|とうてん}の{代|か}わりに{中黒|なかぐろ}を{使|つか}うことがある。
examples.english: When listing parallel terms, an interpunct is sometimes used instead of a comma.

notes:
Also called {中点|なかてん} or {中ポツ|なかぽつ}. The character {中|なか} means "middle" and {黒|ぐろ} means "black (dot)," describing its appearance as a dot positioned in the middle of the line.

USAGE:
The {中黒|なかぐろ} (・) serves several functions in Japanese writing:
- Separating items in a list: {赤|あか}・{青|あお}・{黄|き}
- Marking word boundaries in katakana: マイケル・ジャクソン
- Separating parallel or contrasting items: {和|わ}・{洋|よう}
- Indicating date components: 2024・3・15

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中黒|なかぐろ}で{区切|くぎ}る — to separate with an interpunct
- {中黒|なかぐろ}を{打|う}つ — to type/insert an interpunct
- {中黒|なかぐろ}{区切|くぎ}り — interpunct-delimited

RELATED WORDS:
- {読点|とうてん} — comma (、); the standard Japanese comma
- {句点|くてん} — period (。); the Japanese full stop
- {中点|なかてん} — interpunct; an alternative name for the same mark
